boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten nearby corridor stops with a specific, source-backed reason to look closer.

cards.title: Howard Theatre
cards.subtitle: T Street NW corridor, just south of campus
cards.notes: Check the theatre calendar before walking down T Street, then photograph the restored marquee from the public sidewalk.
cards.short_summary: A historic performance venue on the T Street approach to Shaw.
cards.evidence_claim: The Howard Theatre is at 620 T Street NW and presents live entertainment.
cards.access_notes: Event entry, ticketing, and age policies vary; confirm the listing before attending.

cards.title: 9:30 Club
cards.subtitle: V Street NW corridor, south of Howard
cards.notes: Use V Street as the route and check the show page in advance; the official FAQ gives the venue address and Metro exit.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed live-music venue along V Street.
cards.evidence_claim: 9:30 Club lists its address as 815 V Street NW and directs visitors toward the 10th Street Metro exit.
cards.access_notes: Tickets and event-specific age policies apply; verify the individual show before making plans.

cards.title: Busboys and Poets at 14th & V
cards.subtitle: 14th Street NW corridor at V Street
cards.notes: Walk the 14th Street stretch to the 14th-and-V location; check its current events listing for readings or discussions.
cards.short_summary: A bookstore, restaurant, and events stop on the 14th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Busboys and Poets lists its 14th & V location at 2021 14th Street NW and publishes upcoming events there.
cards.source_title: Busboys and Poets Contact and Locations
cards.access_notes: Food, books, and some events may require purchase or tickets; review the event listing.

cards.title: African American Civil War Memorial
cards.subtitle: U Street NW corridor at 10th Street and Vermont Avenue
cards.notes: Approach via U Street and use the outdoor memorial as a self-guided history stop; pair it with the nearby museum when available.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor memorial at the U Street and Vermont Avenue junction.
cards.evidence_claim: The memorial stands at Vermont Avenue, 10th Street, and U Street NW; it is outdoors, open 24 hours, and self-guided.
cards.source_title: National Park Service — African American Civil War Memorial: Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial is open 24 hours; staffing and adjacent-museum hours differ.

cards.entity_name: African American Civil War Memorial Museum
cards.title: African American Civil War Memorial Museum
cards.subtitle: Vermont Avenue NW corridor, across from the U Street memorial
cards.notes: Take Vermont Avenue to the museum entrance and confirm exhibit status before going; the official page currently notes an indoor-exhibit closure.
cards.short_summary: A museum documenting the United States Colored Troops beside U Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum at 1925 Vermont Avenue NW honors the roles of 209,145 United States Colored Troops; admission is free with a suggested donation.
cards.source_title: African American Civil War Memorial Museum — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: The official visitor page says the indoor exhibit is closed; check reopening information before visiting.

cards.title: Lincoln Theatre
cards.subtitle: U Street NW corridor near 12th Street
cards.notes: Walk U Street to view the theatre façade, then use the official calendar if you want to plan a performance around the corridor.
cards.short_summary: A historic theatre whose official site connects it to U Street’s cultural history.
cards.evidence_claim: Lincoln Theatre is at 1215 U Street NW, and its official site identifies the theatre and Duke Ellington as legacies of the U Street Corridor.
cards.access_notes: Box-office and event access vary; tickets may be required for performances.

cards.title: Ben's Chili Bowl
cards.subtitle: U Street NW corridor at 1213 U Street
cards.notes: Use U Street to find the original location and read its posted history; confirm current service status before making a food stop.
cards.short_summary: A long-running U Street restaurant with documented civil-rights-era history.
cards.evidence_claim: Ben's Chili Bowl identifies its U Street location as 1213 U Street NW and says the business began on U Street in 1958.
cards.access_notes: Food and drink purchases are required; check the restaurant’s current location page for availability.

cards.entity_name: Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site
cards.title: Carter G. Woodson Home
cards.subtitle: 9th Street NW corridor in Shaw
cards.notes: Follow 9th Street to see Woodson’s office-home from the public way, and check the park page before planning an interior visit.
cards.short_summary: The former office-home central to Woodson’s Black-history scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies 1538 9th Street NW as Woodson’s office-home and the headquarters of ASALH and Associated Publishers.
cards.source_title: National Park Service — Carter G. Woodson Home NHS
cards.access_notes: NPS says the site is temporarily closed for construction; exterior viewing should respect posted restrictions.

cards.entity_name: Mary McLeod Bethune Council House National Historic Site
cards.title: Mary McLeod Bethune Council House
cards.subtitle: Vermont Avenue NW corridor at 1318 Vermont
cards.notes: Walk Vermont Avenue to the historic townhouse and use the official tour information to choose an available public-visit day.
cards.short_summary: Bethune’s last Washington home and the first NCNW headquarters.
cards.evidence_claim: The Council House at 1318 Vermont Avenue NW was the first headquarters of the National Council of Negro Women and Mary McLeod Bethune’s last Washington home.
cards.source_title: National Park Service — Mary McLeod Bethune Council House
cards.access_notes: The NPS states that historic-house tours are open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays; verify before travel.

cards.title: DC Go-Go Music Corner Mural
cards.subtitle: Florida Avenue NW corridor at 7th Street NW
cards.notes: Walk Florida Avenue to 7th Street for the public mural and use it as a visual introduction to the District’s go-go culture.
cards.short_summary: A city-supported public mural at the 7th and Florida go-go corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The District announced a go-go mural installation at its designated Go-Go Music Corner at 7th Street and Florida Avenue NW.
cards.source_title: District of Columbia — Go-Go Music Corner mural announcement
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public-art stop; observe from public space and follow any temporary streetscape notices.
